text: mike: Heads-up — customer `Payluma` (prod) reports consistent 429s from /v1/rerank over the last 30m. They say it started after a spike in candidate generation. They provided request_id: req_97a2b and a sample response: `HTTP/1.1 429 Too Many Requests\nContent-Type: application/json\n{ \"error\": { \"type\": \"rate_limited\", \"message\": \"quota exceeded for rerank_route\", \"code\": \"rerank_quota_exceeded\" } }`. Putting logs below. :frowning:
messages: anita: thx mike. quick question — is this only the rerank endpoint or are they seeing any 429s on generate/embed?

mike: only rerank according to their telemetry. embedding/generate fine. They said 20 req/s for rerank burst, previous steady state ~5 req/s. They called it a two-minute outage for their UI (users see blank results).
devon: tagging infra-oncall — @devon — rolling window quotas could be kicking in. mike, can you paste the raw request headers (no PII) and a minimal repro?

mike: pasted their curl (sanitized):

````bash
curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/rerank \
  -H 'Authorization: Bearer sk-prod-REDACTED' \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -d '{"query": "best wireless earbuds", "candidates": ["item1...", "item2...", "item3..."], "top_k": 5}'
````

Response header includes `Retry-After: 30` and body as above. They say retries with basic backoff still hit 429 until ~1 min later.

anita: interesting — rerank is high QPS but low token count usually. The quota configuration for rerank was recently tweaked (last week) when we added per-route buckets. Possible mis-mapping of rerank -> embedding bucket. can someone check route->quota mapping for customer org Payluma?

devon: checking routing config now. I see a policy that maps /v1/rerank to bucket `batching_v1` for most orgs, but enterprise override should map to `large_qps`. Payluma is enterprise but their org tag on our side looks like `payluma-prod` and might not match override. that would route them to the lower quota.
mike: customer says they have Dedicated trial — they expected higher throughput. They pasted account id 788112. Also pasted server-side request_id list: [req_97a2b, req_97a2c, req_97a2d].

sarah: from billing/entitlement — org 788112 has Dedicated add-on but the org label in control plane is `payluma` (no `-prod`). There's a mismatch. I can add an alias mapping to match `payluma-prod` -> `payluma` but want infra to confirm this will switch their routing bucket.

devon: alias mapping will help. I'll apply a temporary override mapping `payluma-prod` -> large_qps bucket. Giving a heads-up: changes take effect in routing config within ~30s but existing in-flight rate counters may still throttle until the quota window resets.
mike: telling customer ETA ~2-3 min. their PM is pretty upset — asking for credit. :anguished:
anita: additional note: rerank requests are counted as "requests" not tokens, so large candidate lists (n>50) spike request CPU & count toward qps. We should ask customer for candidate counts.
mike: they replied — typical candidates 40-80 for the batch, occasionally 200 for internal testing. That likely explains the burst. their UI does 200 candidates then top_k=5.

devon: rollback plan — apply alias mapping now, then monitor the `quota_decisions` logs for org 788112. Also add temporary per-org soft-limit: allow tokenless rerank up to 100rps for 5m. I'll run the change and paste logs.
ops-bot: deploy started by devon at 2026-03-15T17:21:10Z — routing override apply(payluma-prod -> payluma).

devon: override applied. watch logs:
````
2026-03-15T17:21:38Z [router] org=788112 route=/v1/rerank quota=large_qps decision=allow reason=alias_applied
2026-03-15T17:21:40Z [quota] org=788112 current_rps=82 limit=100 action=allow
````
mike: customer reports success — rerank calls recovered after ~45s. No more 429s in the last 3m. They asked what caused it to break without warning.

anita: root cause summary for now: org label mismatch caused enterprise override not to apply; routing fallback used the lower quota bucket causing 429s under burst. Secondary factor: unusually high candidate counts (200) pushed request rate and CPU usage up. For remediation: 1) fix alias mapping (done), 2) add monitoring alert for abrupt per-org 429 spike on rerank, 3) docs: recommend preferring candidate filtering server-side to keep lists <= 50 or use batching, 4) infra: consider dynamic bucket mapping fallback that promotes enterprise orgs when entitlement exists.
sarah: billing — customer requested credit for downtime. recommend 10% of last month usage for the ~2 min outage? assigning to account exec.

mike: I'll draft postmortem & send to customer with proposed credit. Also adding repro steps for eng: minimal curl above + a script that fires 150 concurrent rerank requests with 200 candidates to reproduce. putting repro snippet: 
````bash
for i in {1..150}; do \
  curl -sS -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/rerank -H 'Authorization: Bearer sk-REDACTED' -d '{"query":"x","candidates": ["c1","c2",...],"top_k":5}' &
done; wait
````

devon: good. Follow-ups for infra: (a) ensure route->quota mapping logs include org label and alias resolution (b) surface `Retry-After` and quota bucket name in 429 body to help customers debug (c) run a sweep to detect org label mismatches from onboarding scripts. I'll open tickets.

anita: optional longer-term: consider a dedicated 'rerank_high_qps' path that implements fast-path batching/kvcache so large candidate lists don't spike routing counts. I'll prototype after tickets are triaged.

mike: closing loop — customer happy for now, asked for timeline on infra fixes. I'll set expectation: alias cleanup + monitoring today; infra tickets for code changes in next sprint. Thanks everyone. :tada:
devon: I'll create infra ticket INF-4398 and link here. ops-bot notes: INF-4398 created by devon — investigate route alias resolution and expose quota bucket in 429.
sarah: I'll handle the credit request and ping account exec.
